title: SSE sentinel frames and client-agnostic reconnect handshake
creator: Marco Li
description: Introduce a lightweight sentinel-frame based protocol extension and a minimal reconnect handshake so that a single server stream implementation can interoperate with a wide range of clients (browser EventSource, proxy middleboxes, mobile SDKs, and older polyglot codebases). Goal: avoid expensive full-state replay on reconnect while retaining strict tool/function-call and structured-output boundaries.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Server emits an optional 1-2 byte sentinel frame that marks semantic boundaries (tool-call start/end, structured output chunk) without changing existing text/event-stream semantics.
2) Clients that understand sentinel frames can resume mid-stream using a short resume token; legacy clients ignore sentinel frames and continue to receive textual events unchanged.
3) Reconnect handshake documented and validated with at least three client implementations (browser EventSource, node fetch EventSource polyfill, mobile SDK).
4) End-to-end tests show <1% increase in median latency and no regressions in function-call atomicity on reconnect.
5) Drifted partial tokens are reconciled with a checksum/sequence approach and documented recovery steps.
implementation_plan:
1) Define sentinel frame bytes and encoding: single-line event named 'sn' with base64 payload describing {seq, type, boundary_tag, crc}.
2) Server: emit sentinel event immediately before/after logical boundaries (function call open/close, structured JSONL output boundary).
3) Resume token generation: compact string containing last-seen seq and short soft-checksum; store per-session in in-memory cache and optional durable log for dedicated/private.
4) Reconnect handshake: client includes 'X-Resume-Token' header; server validates token and replies with 200 + 'X-Resume-Mode: accept|fallback' or 409 for incompatible.
5) Compatibility shim: server can be configured to run in strict, best-effort, or legacy mode. Legacy mode filters sentinel events so they appear as noop comments for legacy clients.
6) Add instrumentation: counters for resume success/fail, average replay length, sentinel-emitted-per-minute, and reconnect latency.
7) Ship tests and SDK helpers (JS/Go) that parse sentinel frames and build resume tokens.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: Middleboxes may drop non-UTF-8 bytes; mitigation: sentinel is encoded as valid UTF-8 base64 inside a normal SSE 'sn' event.
- Risk: Resume tokens leak sensitive state; mitigation: sign tokens with HMAC using per-tenant key and short TTL.
- Risk: Ambiguity between sentinel and text content in function-call payloads; mitigation: emit sentinel only as distinct SSE events (event: sn) never as data payload inside a functioncall event.
- Risk: Increased complexity for small clients; mitigation: default legacy compatibility mode and provide SDK helpers that are small (single-file).
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for encoder/decoder, resume-token validation, and CRC mismatch paths.
- Integration tests: simulated intermittent network with deterministic packet drops to verify resume acceptance and fallback.
- Cross-client matrix: run browser EventSource, node eventsource polyfill, Python requests-compatible streaming, and mobile SDK in CI.
- Load test: verify sentinel emission under 10k concurrent streams with <3% CPU overhead.
- Chaos test: inject altered resume tokens to confirm graceful fallback to streaming-from-start and proper metrics emitted.

2026-02-28: Defined token format and HMAC signing strategy in design doc; reviewed with security and infra.
2026-03-05: Compatibility shim options added to dedicated config; initial JS SDK helper sketch completed.
2026-03-11: Began interop tests with browser EventSource; observed middlebox dropping when sent raw binary — switched to base64-in-event approach.
blockers: KMS access for signing tokens (security team gating)
Dedicated config flag rollout coordination with infra team
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on: token entropy and TTL choices, the exact set of fields emitted in 'sn' sentinel events, and the server-mode semantics (strict/best-effort/legacy). We should also validate that the checksum algorithm is fast and collision-resistant for short sequences.
next_steps: 1) Resolve KMS gating with Security by 2026-03-16. 2) Finalize JS/Go SDK helpers and publish alpha packages. 3) Run full interop matrix and sign off on runbook for resume-fallback incident handling.
customer_notes: This feature reduces full-session replays for short disconnects and preserves tool/function-call atomicity across reconnects for supported clients. Legacy clients will continue to work unchanged, but won't benefit from resume semantics until SDKs are updated.
final_acceptance_checks:
- Resume token HMAC verified in at least two environments.
- SDKs parse sentinel events and produce resume requests.
- Metrics show <2% of reconnects result in full replay in canary.
